Center]] |champion = |tourney = |tourney_result = }} {{2020–21 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2020–21 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Louisville]] during the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team played its home games on Denny Crum Court at the [[KFC Yum! Center]] in [[Downtown Louisville|downtown Louisville, Kentucky]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. They were led by third-year head coach [[Chris Mack (basketball)|Chris Mack]]. In a season limited due to the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]], the Cardinals finished the season 13–7, 8–5 to finish in seventh place in [[2020–21 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]]. They lost to [[2020–21 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] in the second round of the [[2021 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]]. They were listed as an alternate team for the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] if a team were unable to participate due to COVID-19 issues.{{cite web|url=https://gocards.com/news/2021/3/15/louisville-is-first-alternate-for-ncaa-mens-basketball-tournament.aspx|title=Louisville is First Alternate for NCAA men's basketball tournament}} The team declined an invitation to the [[2021 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]] prior to the NCAA tournament field being announced.{{cite web|url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/ncaabk/ncaa-tournament-snubs-louisville-duke-among-teams-to-turn-down-nit/ar-BB1eAa0F|title=NCAA tournament snubs Louisville, Duke among teams to turn down NIT|publisher=[[Yahoo! Sports]]}}{{Cite web|last=Russell|first=Shannon|title=Louisville basketball denied bid into 2021 NCAA Tournament, won't accept NIT invite|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2021/03/14/ncaa-tournament-2021-louisville-basketball-opponent-bracket/4624932001/|access-date=2021-09-16|website=The Courier-Journal|language=en-US}} When all teams were able to participate in the opening rounds of the NCAA tournament, the Cardinals season ended.{{Cite web|last=Conway|first=Tyler|title=All 68 2021 NCAA Tournament Teams Cleared to Play After COVID-19 Testing|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2936685-all-68-2021-ncaa-tournament-teams-cleared-to-play-after-covid-19-testing|access-date=2021-09-16|website=Bleacher Report|language=en}} ==Previous season== The [[2019–20 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Cardinals]] finished the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20 season]] with of 24–7, 15–5 to finish in a tie for second place in [[2019–20 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]]. As the No. 3 seed in the [[2020 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]], they were scheduled to play [[2019–20 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]] before the tournament was canceled due to the COVID-19 pandemic.{{cite web |title=Statement from ACC on Men's Basketball Tournament |url=https://theacc.com/news/2020/3/12/statement-from-acc-on-mens-basketball-tournament.aspx |website=theacc.com |publisher=Atlantic Coast Conference |accessdate=12 March 2020}} The [[2020 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] was later also canceled due to the pandemic.{{Cite web|url=https://www.ncaa.org/about/resources/media-center/news/ncaa-cancels-remaining-winter-and-spring-championships|title=NCAA cancels remaining winter and spring championships|last=|first=|date=|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200312202043/http://www.ncaa.org/about/resources/media-center/news/ncaa-cancels-remaining-winter-and-spring-championships |archive-date=2020-03-12 |access-date=}} ==Offseason== ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" style="text-align:center;" !
